question.text: Under Solon, all Athenian citizens were allowed to participate in the ekklesia assembly that met in a building southwest of this elevated part of the city, which is home to the Parthenon.
question.clue: This site of the Propylaea also featured six women taking the place of columns on its Caryatid Porch.

swap.leadin: Name these people who all formulated their own law codes.
swap.text: This Athenian created Athens' first constitution, whose harshness gave rise to a word meaning "marked by extreme severity or cruelty."
swap.clue: This man was given jurisdiction after Cylon tried to seize power, and the orator Demades joked that this man wrote in blood rather than in ink.

question.text: The Battle of Aegospotami ended this series of wars, which was named for a league led by Sparta. This war was temporarily ended with the Peace of Nicias [NIH-kee-as].
question.clue: One side in this war laid siege to Melos, where a dialogue apocryphally occurred containing the aphorism "the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must."

swap.leadin: This monarch ended the tradition of the wandering Spanish Court when he selected Madrid to be the permanent capital.
swap.text: Name this King of Spain from 1556 to 1598. His faced the Dutch revolt in the Netherlands and was at one point married to England's Queen Mary I.
swap.clue: Another ruler of this name and number won the Third Sacred War against the Phocians as well as the battle of Chaeronea for Macedon.

question.leadin: According to legend, Pheidippides ran 26 miles to report the Greek victory at this battle to Athens.
question.text: Identify this 490 BC battle in which the far outnumbered Greeks under Miltiades defeated the Persian army of Darius the Great.
question.clue: The marshlands around the site of this battle prevented one side from fielding its cavalry, but they still utilized their 10,000 Immortals.

swap.leadin: Because this island was considered the birthplace of Artemis and Apollo, its residents were prohibited from dying and tainting the land, so prisoners were executed on nearby Mykonos.
swap.text: Name this island in the Cyclades which hosted the Athenian treasury and thus lent its name to Athens' alliance of city-states.
swap.clue: Dying in this location was prohibited in a ritual purification during the Peloponnesian War.

question.text: This set of generals divided up Alexander's empire and fought each other for it after his death. They included Ptolemy, Antigonus the One-Eyed, and Seleucus Nicator.
question.clue: Conflict between these people began when their former leader granted his kingdom "to the strongest."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the naval commander Konon.
swap.text: During a war named for this city-state, Konon helped the Persian satrap Pharnabazus secure victory in the Battle of Cnidus. This city-state was sacked by Mummius in 146 BCE and was located on a namesake isthmus.
swap.clue: The King's Peace ended a war named for this city that broke out shortly after the Peloponnesian War and pitted Sparta against a Greek-Persian alliance.

question.text: The congregation of the Archbishop of Candia--modern day Irakloion--were massacred here during the Greek War of Independence. Some artifacts here are written in the Linear A script.
question.clue: Power moved away from the city of Gortyn during Muslim rule of this region.

swap.text: This German's interest in Homer led him to uncover the ruins of Troy and Mycenae.
swap.clue: One of this man's most famous discoveries was a golden burial mask belonging to a Mycenaean king, which this archaeologist presumed was Agamemnon.

question.text: The Helot population comprised almost entirely of residents from the south of this peninsula, where the city of Sparta is located. This peninsula's north contains the city of Delphi.
question.answerHtml: the Peloponnese [or Peloponnesian peninsula or Peloponnesia or Peloponnesus or Morea; prompt on Greek peninsula]
question.clue: On this peninsula, a sealstone "combat agate ("AG-ut")" was left in a possible "Griffin Warrior Tomb" at a "sandy" site where syllabic "oxen tablets" record the palace economy of a wanax.

swap.leadin: A gold funerary mask found at this site was dubbed the "Mask of Agamemnon" by Heinrich Schliemann.
swap.text: Name this archeological site. It names a phase of the Greek bronze age which followed the Minoan civilization and was likely destroyed by the Dorian invasion.
swap.clue: An artifact from this culture depicts a handlebar mustache and beard on a gold burial mask.

question.text: Following his death, Philip II's remains were collected into a Golden Larnax emblazoned with a symbol of this object. The Argead dynasty used an emblem depicting this object as its royal symbol.
question.answerHtml: Vergina Sun [prompt on Star of Vergina or Vergina Star or Argead Star]

swap.leadin: This kingdom's army used 256-man blocks of infantry soldiers called syntagma.
swap.text: Name this kingdom, which defeated an alliance led by Demosthenes at the Battle of Chaeronea in 338 BCE. A later ruler of this kingdom won battles at Issus and Gaugamela.
swap.clue: This kingdom, which was annexed by Rome after the Battle of Pydna, formed a federation of Greek cities called the League of Corinth after it defeated Thebes at the Battle of Chaeronea.

question.leadin: All male citizens were mandated to perform this program except for the firstborn sons of the Eurypontid and Agiad houses.
question.text: Name this rigorous education and military training program employed by Sparta that included the paides, paidiskoi, and hebontes stages for boys starting at the age of 7 until they turned 29.
question.clue: The Eurypontids and Agiads were exempted from this system, which moved top performers to the krypteia ("krip-TAI-uh"), where they would terrorize helots ("HELL-uts").

swap.text: This Spartan general became a hero at Methone. His loss at Pylos led him to abandon several men on the isle of Sphacteria. His death at Amphipolis, along with that of the Athenian Cleon, helped lead to the Peace of Nicias.
swap.clue: In this man's last battle, he led a small force against the Athenian center, after which Clearidas led a larger force against the Athenian right, forcing the Athenians to flee to Eion.

question.leadin: Prior to this battle, the winning commander saw the daughters of Scedasus weeping at their tombs, but instead of sacrifcing a blonde virgin as he was asked, he sacrifced a flly with a red mane that burst into his camp.
question.text: Name this ancient battle which ended with the defeat and death of king Cleombrotus I.
question.clue: The victorious commander here put 50-men-deep columns on his left flank, allowing Pelopidas's men to crush the opposing Royal Bodyguard.

swap.leadin: The engineer Eupalinos blasted a tunnel through Mount Kastro on this island so he could build an aqueduct to supply its capital with water.
swap.text: Name this island ruled in 538 BC by the tyrant Polycrates, who constructed a temple to Hera here dubbed the Heraion.
swap.clue: Herodotus claims that the pharaoh Ahmose broke off Egypt's alliance with this city-state after its tyrant discovered his lost ring in the belly of a fish.

question.text: This Corinthian ruler was a member of the Seven Sages and created a ship's' dragway between the Saronic and Corinthian Gulfs called the Diolkos. The Corcyrans, who didn't want his rule, killed his son Lycophron to prevent them from swapping thrones.
question.clue: This man sent three hundred Corcyran nobles to Alyattes, ruler of Lydia, to be made eunuchs.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Leonidas' predecessor Cleomenes I.
swap.text: Cleomenes I waged war against this other city and defeated it at the Battle of Sepeia in 494 BC. This city earlier defeated Sparta at Hysiae, during which it was ruled by Pheidon.
swap.clue: Weights and measures found at the Heraion of this city are said to date to the reign of King Pheidon, who ruled this city as a tyrant.
